full_judgment: 24. Further case of the prosecution is that if Zubair did not show the house of Dr. Azad to the 5 Al-Badars, Dr Azad could not be kidnapped and that he also misled P.W.1 Habibul Bashar telling him that Al-Badars had taken his brother to the residence of Hajee Kashem. But he was not taken there. Thereby Zubair frustrated the efforts of Habibul Bashar to help rescue his brother from the custody of Al-Badars who were still then in the micro bus on the rea to the south of the south gate and Zubair intentionally did so because he belonged to the Al-Badars being a student of Alia Madrasa and a member of Islamic Chatra Sangha. The defence seriously disputes these charges against Zubair. It is first to be seen if Zubair belonged to the Al-Badars and was a member of “Islamic Chatra Sangha”. In corroboration of the charge that Zubair was a member of Islamic Chatra Sangha which was affiliated to reactionary political parties, namely Jamaat-e-Islami, Muslim League e.t.c. who were against the Bangladesh movement. The prosecution examined PW 23 Sikandar Mia who was a man of Laksham in the district of Comilla. His evidence is that he was a rickshaw puller. But he gave up that profession and started selling ‘Pan’ from August, 1971. He used to sell ‘Pan’ and cigarettes in front of the medical college hostel at Bakshibazar in September/October 1971. There was a conference in Alia Madrasha where he saw Zubair with a rifle in hand and in Khaki uniform and a cap on his head. He saw him at Alia Madrasha gate. The witness further deposed that he worked as a domestic servant in the house of Zubair’s uncle near the house of Zubair in Daira Sharif. In cross-examination the witness failed to state the date and the period of the conference at Alia Madrasha. He could not also say the purpose of the conference. It may be noted here that Zubair was not sent up in the charge sheet which was submitted on 20th April 1972 against the other two prisoners. But under direction of the superior officer the IO PW26 filed a supplementary charge sheet against Zubair on 16th of June 1972. PW 23 Sekandar Mia was examined by the IO on 30th July after submission of the supplementary charge sheet. It is difficult to follow why such an important witness for the prosecution could not be found out by the IO before the submission of the supplementary charge sheet. It is strange that after submission of the charge sheet and the supplementary charge sheet, evidence was still being collected. This certainly goes to show that unusual procedure was adopted by the prosecution in the case. The evidence of the IO shows that Mr. Jalaluddin was the Principal of Alia Madrasha. He was residing in the quarters within Alia Madrasha. He was examined by the IO and was also charge sheet witness. He was a competent person to say if there was any conference of Islami Chatra Sangha in September/October in Alia Madrasha and whether Zubair was a member of Islamic Chatra Sangha. It is not denied that Zubair was a student of Alia Madrasha. That does not necessarily mean that he was a member of Islamic Chatra Sangha. The best evidence was withheld by the prosecution. The presumption must go against the prosecution u/s 114 illustration (g) of the Evidence Act. Another piece of evidence to show that Zubiar was an Al-Badar are two photographs (exts 1 and 2). Ext 1 is a group photograph and ext 2 is a passport size photograph. PW 1 himself expressed his inability to connect Zubair with the passport size photograph. The group photograph (ext 1) contains the photos of some persons including that of Zubair. The photo of one Nurul Haq is said to be an Al-Badar and a case against him is said to be pending. Simply because the photo of Nurul Haq said to be an Al-Badar is there with that of Zubair the process through which this photograph was collected sets one to thinking. The police seized the photograph from the office of PW 1 Habibul Bashar. With this photograph PW25 Raisuddin Bhuiyan went to PW 24 Fazlul Karim a News Editor, Dainik Bangla a few days after the liberation for publication stating that this was the photograph of Al-Badars. PW24 advised PW25 Raisuddin Bhuyan first to lodge a general Diary at the Thana. Accordingly PW 24 lodged a General Diary, Ext 8 at the Thana and thereafter it was published in the Dainik Bangla PW 24 in cross examination on behalf of Zubair said that at the time many people had given such photographs but they did not publish all. He could not; however, recollect as to who produced which photographs and when there is no evidence on the side of the prosecution in which year and at what time the group photograph was taken. The prisoner himself has stated while examined u/s 342 Cr. P.C that in 1969 AD he had gone to Sylhet along with some other students and a Lecturer. This group photograph was taken there. There is nothing to controvert this statement of Zubair. We, therefore, accept this statement that this group photograph was taken in the year 1969 A.D. when the formation of Al-Badars Razakars, etc., was not in the imagination of any person.
